sealed_candidate.answer: ## Decision support — Does the packet prove a ≥20% total-cost reduction from agent-assisted delivery? (Fictional Aster Enterprise fixture, fictional data; not real-world guidance.)

claims.text: The packet does not quantify a causal total-cost change of at least 20%; the threshold is not established by the supplied evidence.
claims.uncertainty: No material uncertainty that the packet lacks the required measurement; the direction and magnitude of any real cost effect remain unmeasured, not merely unproven.

claims.text: The only quantitative datum in the packet is 40 accepted pull requests in one month, reported with no task mix, control group, reviewer hours, failure count, or provider costs.
claims.uncertainty: None regarding packet contents; any underlying cost effect of the pilot is unmeasured.

claims.text: The supplied measurement policy requires evaluation via matched tasks, quality gates, human review time, rework, elapsed lead time, and total cost; it requires counting failed or abandoned tasks and explicitly disallows inferring causal benefit from accepted-PR counts.
claims.uncertainty: None; the policy text is explicit.

claims.text: The required matched comparison with complete cost and failure accounting is absent: no comparable baseline and no total-cost numerator or denominator exist in the packet, so the implementation-evidence obligation is unresolved.
claims.uncertainty: The absence is certain within the supplied pack; closure would require new measurement (matched tasks, review hours, rework, failures, provider cost), not interpretation of existing text.

claims.text: Contradiction preserved: the pilot note's headline metric (accepted PRs) is the same metric the measurement policy disallows as a causal or cost proxy, and the pilot note contains none of the policy's required measurements; no supplied source reconciles this tension.
claims.uncertainty: The contradiction is unresolved within the packet and is reported as supplied.

claims.text: Using accepted pull requests as a cost proxy is excluded from this analysis, consistent with the decision request and with the supplied policy's prohibition on inferring causal benefit from accepted-PR counts.

Bounded abstention applies: the evidence cannot support the requested decision, and an affirmative answer would require inventing missing measurements (baseline, cost accounting, failure counts, provider costs).
claims.uncertainty: None regarding the abstention itself; the underlying cost effect is unmeasured and left unresolved.
